frequency_question: How often do major central banks activate or raise the countercyclical capital buffer above 0% outside of immediate post-implementation rollout phases?
membership_rule: Members are G20 or Basel Committee jurisdictions that formally instituted a CCyB framework and subsequently moved the active requirement above 0% in response to perceived systemic risk build-up. Excluded are passive introductory periods where buffers were set to 0% as a default without active tightening cycles.

cases.name: Bank of England Financial Policy Committee CCyB activation
Reserve Bank of New Zealand OCR and capital buffer tightening
Norges Bank countercyclical capital buffer hike

provenance_note: claims 18 cases from only 3 named (6.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 3 named anchor episodes; estimated approximately 18 distinct advanced economy implementation cycles matching criteria.
known_gaps: Excludes smaller emerging market jurisdictions with non-comparable credit-to-GDP gaps.
skeleton: Selected G20 and advanced economy jurisdictions with institutionalized macroprudential mandates observed over rolling 18-month policy windows during non-crisis credit expansions.
multiplier: 3 activations observed across 18 relevant jurisdictions over a decade of post-crisis operation, yielding an empirical baseline frequency of approximately 16% for any given multi-year window.
validity_reason: Basel III structural implementation frameworks remain stable through the medium term.
